detail.runner_up_case: The strongest honest case for FALSE is an evidentiary-sufficiency attack, not an affirmative disproof. Every Q3 source in the file is weak: Wikipedia is tertiary; the Instagram and Facebook posts are undated social media; and the 26gambitchambers.com blog carries a publication date of 2026-10-06, which post-dates the 2026-10-01 as-of date and therefore cannot count as evidence as of today. No primary record has been pulled at all - no UK Companies House administration filing, no US bankruptcy docket, no dated wire report (Reuters/FT/BBC). The sources also disagree on mechanics ($50M vs $37M seized; 'announced insolvency proceedings' vs 'filed for bankruptcy'), a pattern consistent with an announcement hardening into a completed filing through repetition rather than verification. 'Announced insolvency proceedings' is materially different from 'entered insolvency proceedings': a company can announce an intention to appoint administrators while a rescue, sale, or creditor deal is still being negotiated. If the formal process was never commenced, or only a subsidiary (e.g., a US entity) petitioned while the UK parent continued, the flat claim 'Builder.ai entered insolvency proceedings in 2025' would be materially wrong or at best qualified. Identity, too, rests only on Wikipedia/Wikidata; confusion between the Engineer.ai Corporation entities (UK vs US vs Singapore/India subsidiaries) has not been excluded. On this record, FALSE (or at minimum UNVERIFIABLE) cannot be ruled out - though it must be conceded that the convergence of independent secondary sources makes FALSE the less likely verdict.
